_comment: A machine that comes back from a stop must come back whole (#549), and
the replay that brings it back must be idempotent (#498).
Both measured on 2026-08-27 on the Scaleway example stack under --vm
incus-ovn, and they are one spec because they are one path: the address
replay a restart runs is what shouted the ERROR.

mutations.label: #549: a restarted guest stops being given back the routes to its peered subnets, so it comes back running, on its address, reaching its own subnet and nothing one router away

mutations.label: #549, the ownership half: the repair stops asking whether the network is one the emulator created, and reads the gateway of an operator's own bridge to write a route inside a guest through it
#549, the mode half: the bridge mode starts laying OVN aggregates, pointing a guest's private traffic at an address no router answers on

mutations.label: #498: the replay stops noticing that a routed NIC already delivers the address, so it delegates the same /32 to the uplink where the routed NIC's own host route already sits, and shouts an ERROR over a correct host
#498, the accepting half: every address reads as already delivered, so an address that genuinely needs the OVN path never gets it and the machine answers on nothing
